item.title: Cardi B Snaps On Mona Love For Throwing Her Under The Bus As Colorism Dispute Explodes Online
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B challenged Mona's colorism criticism and said the podcaster had privately sought her advice on career moves and brand deals.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B challenged Mona Love’s colorism criticism by claiming the podcaster had asked her for career help for years.

Mona, also known as Don’t Call Me White Girl, revisited a 13-second clip from Cardi’s 15-minute Instagram Live in 2024. Cardi responded on X, saying women with lighter skin had an edge, but skin tone alone couldn’t explain her success.

Cardi said colorism shaped jobs, the justice system and how men treated women in strip clubs. But she said talent, steady work, marketing, showing up and knowing your audience also mattered. She recalled people mocking her teeth, acne, braids, speech and stripping.

“When I worked in the strip club, I seen how men treated me and how they treated dark skin women… I can never dismiss how colorism affects dark skin women and men in general. Not just in the work place but in the justice system as well. And I have stood up for it plenty of times . But what Im always going to stand up for is that my skin tone is not solely the reason for my success,” Cardi B fumed.

She said Mona had sent her messages for years about surgery, career advice, brand deals and pitches. Cardi asked why Mona used the short clip instead of reaching out. She also accused Mona of trying to shift attention from criticism over her remarks about Tia Kemp’s comedy credentials.

“You went out your way to make a video with no context when this wasnt even a topic on no blogs and no platforms.. literally nobody was talking about this. Why would you go on your platform to talk about something you were misinformed about instead of doing your due diligence or at least hitting me up like you do about anything else? I know why … because you decided to use me and a sensitive topic as a scapegoat. a topic I havent talked about in years that you randomly brought up. And now im getting dragged for it. You used me as shield because you was under fire for the backlash you was getting for talking about Tia Kemp another black woman all because she was selling more tickets than you!” Cardi B said.

Mona had raised that argument with her TikTok followers. She said lighter skin and Dominican heritage could help Cardi get brand deals over a darker-skinned woman with the same talent.

“Colorism is real, racism is real,” Mona said on TikTok. She did not cast herself as an exception. Mona told followers that both she and Cardi likely benefited from colorism. She also said she was a fan and praised Cardi’s talent. Her point was about access to work, not a lack of skill.

Cardi faced a similar debate in April 2024. Influencer Raymonte Cole asked why he was seen as too “ghetto” to work with brands while she got deals. He pointed to her lighter skin.

At the time, Cardi said she had changed to work with brands. “I had to change the way I talk, the way I act and the way I respond and how I present myself,” she wrote on X.

Her voice became a separate target that June. As AllHipHop previously reported, Cardi answered people mocking her speech on X on June 3, 2024.

“I will never change the way I talk,” she wrote. “I became famous from that, just being myself!”

item.title: Gunna Concert Attendee Pleads Guilty After Busting Nut On Woman
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Gunna concert attendee Glendon Marshall admits a public decency offense as a separate sexual assault charge awaits his plea.
item.content:encoded:
Gunna concert attendee Glendon Marshall pleaded guilty to outraging public decency after e########## on a woman during the rapper’s March show at London’s O2 Arena.

Marshall, 23, of Northolt, appeared at Woolwich Crown Court in southeast London on Monday, November 2, according to local reports.

A second charge accuses Marshall of sexual assault by touching, but he has not entered his plea on that count.

The woman was in her 20s and said the man ejaculated on her leg after approaching her from behind during the March 25 show.

That night had been a long-awaited chance to see Gunna perform, according to the account she later shared on Instagram.

“I’ve been waiting for years to see Gunna perform, and people that know me know how much I love him,” she wrote.

Her posts described the distress that followed and included footage of security staff leading a man away from the concert.

The Metropolitan Police said venue managers called officers at about 8:20 P.M., after staff had detained a man inside the Greenwich arena.

Police already at the venue made the arrest, while officers with special training supported the woman after her report.

The arena described what happened as an “isolated incident” in its initial response to reports about the assault during the show.

AllHipHop covered that arrest in March, when the case was still under investigation, and the allegations had not reached Monday’s plea.

The O2 said its staff and police responded promptly, and the venue pledged to help investigators following the incident.

“Our priority is always the safety and wellbeing of our guests and we are assisting with their inquiries,” an O2 spokesman said.

The show was part of Gunna’s Wun World Tour, which included two London stops and a Manchester date during its European run.

The O2’s event listing placed his London performances on March 25 and March 31, six days apart at the same arena.

Marshall’s case was adjourned until later in November, with the court report giving no exact return date.

item.title: Michael Jackson’s Sons Want Neverland To Help Children Again, Report Says
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Michael Jackson's sons reportedly hoped Neverland could serve children again, as owner Ron Burkle welcomed the prospect of charity events.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Jackson‘s sons Prince and Bigi want Neverland Ranch to help children again, a family source says. The private estate’s owner remains open to hosting charity events.

A source close to the family told Page Six in a November 1 report that the brothers hoped to preserve their father’s former home and its charitable role. The source said Bigi, previously known as Blanket, did not want it turned into a major tourist attraction.

Neither brother owns or controls the property. Businessman Ron Burkle bought it in 2020.

“While Neverland remains a private residence, Ron continues to welcome opportunities to host charitable events there,” Burkle’s spokesperson told Page Six.

The spokesperson also said Jackson’s children and family were welcome to visit. Representatives for Prince and Bigi did not respond to the outlet’s requests for comment.

Prince already has a charity operation of his own through the Heal Los Angeles Foundation, which he co-founded.

The group focuses on education and self-care for young people. It began working directly with Loreto Street Elementary in northeast Los Angeles in 2021 and wants to follow students into middle and high school.

“It’s up to each and every one of us to recognize issues within our current communities and address them with passion and conviction,” Prince wrote on the foundation’s website.

Its fundraising events have used another Jackson family home, Hayvenhurst in Encino. King of Popcorn gives supporters access to that normally private property, with memorabilia tied to Michael’s work on display. The foundation’s 2026 “This Is Thriller” benefit was listed for October 24 at Los Angeles’ Palace Theatre.

Pieces of Neverland’s past have also changed hands. In 2021, 28 statues from the property were offered for sale by a private collector as a single lot.

Make-A-Wish Greater Bay Area documented the ranch’s earlier role in hosting children through the story of a young fan also named Michael.

He visited with his parents and eight other wish families. Jackson guided them around the grounds, where they watched “Aladdin,” played arcade games and had a barbecue lunch. The children also went on carnival rides and left with boxes of Neverland souvenirs.

“It was worth the wait,” the young fan told the charity after meeting his idol.

item.title: Lil Durk Reportedly Sent To Solitary For “Talking Back”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lil Durk was reportedly moved to isolation after questioning jail searches while he pursued release ahead of a second trial.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Durk was moved to solitary confinement Friday at Los Angeles’ Metropolitan Detention Center after allegedly questioning repeated cell searches, according to TMZ.

Sources told the outlet he was reprimanded for “talking back.” A Bureau of Prisons spokesperson said, “we do not discuss the conditions of confinement for any individual in our custody.”

His lawyers had already challenged a long stretch in isolation earlier this year.

In January, attorney Christy O’Connor said Durk had spent 131 days in the special housing unit since August 29, 2025, over an allegedly unauthorized Apple Watch.

The defense asked for a hearing on those conditions and questioned the process used to keep him isolated. The lawyers described a schedule of 23 hours a day in his cell, one phone call a month and no in-person visits at that time.

“The deleterious effects of extended solitary confinement on an inmate’s psychological well-being are well-documented,” O’Connor said.

The latest housing report also came while Durk was seeking release following his September 11 acquittal on five murder-for-hire and stalking counts. He remained in custody on separate charges of murder in aid of racketeering and a firearm offense, to which he pleaded not guilty.

His defense asked Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald to reconsider detention and offered future royalties, publishing revenue, touring income and earnings from his name and image as security, alongside cash and property from supporters.

“Mr. Banks offers to encumber each of these future income streams,” his lawyers wrote in the bond proposal.

Sony also offered to guarantee an appearance bond of up to $1 million.

Andrea Robinson, the mother of Saviay’a “Lul Pab” Robinson, said in a letter she would not object if the court determined bond was appropriate.

Jay-Z, J. Cole, Michael Rubin and Kim Foxx also submitted letters supporting release.

The remaining case concerns the August 19, 2022 shooting near Los Angeles’ Beverly Center that killed Lul Pab. Prosecutors alleged Quando Rondo was the intended target.

Judge Fitzgerald moved the second trial from October 5 to August 30, 2027, giving the defense more time to prepare.

That work included reviewing hundreds of gigabytes of evidence and roughly 30,000 pages of documents. Durk consented to the delay and waived his speedy-trial rights.

item.title: Juan Atkins Dies At 64; His Cybotron Sound Powered Missy Elliott’s “Lose Control”
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Juan Atkins died at 64, leaving a Detroit techno legacy that reached Hip-Hop through Cybotron and Missy Elliott's "Lose Control."
item.content:encoded:
Juan Atkins, the Detroit producer who helped create techno and whose work with Cybotron became part of Missy Elliott’s “Lose Control,” has died at 64.

His agency, Greensmith Artists, confirmed his death to Resident Advisor on November 1. The agency said he was found unresponsive in a Mexico City hotel room before a planned appearance at YuYu Cine Club and was pronounced dead after being taken to a hospital.

For Hip-Hop listeners, one of the clearest routes into Atkins’ catalog was Cybotron’s “Clear.” Its electronic pulse became the foundation for Elliott’s 2005 single “Lose Control,” carrying a record from Detroit’s early electronic scene into another generation’s clubs and playlists.

Elliott produced the single herself. AllHipHop’s 2005 review of The Cookbook pointed to its electro-funk sound, a connection that went back more than two decades to Cybotron’s 1983 recording.

Atkins formed Cybotron with Richard Davis in 1980. The pair drew from Kraftwerk and Parliament-Funkadelic, using synthesizers and electronic percussion to blend funk with a vision of the future.

Born in Detroit and raised in nearby Belleville, Atkins met Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson before the three became known as the Belleville Three. Their records helped turn Detroit into a center for electronic music, with a sound that traveled far beyond Michigan.

Atkins also built a home for that music. He launched Metroplex in 1985 and released “No UFOs” as Model 500 that year. His “Techno Music” later appeared on the 1988 British compilation Techno! The New Dance Sound Of Detroit, helping establish the name that followed the music around the world.

In a 2024 Rolling Stone interview, Atkins remembered how Detroit listeners encountered the sound before they knew it as techno.

“Nobody knew that it was techno music. Especially the Black kids in Detroit. All they knew was that this was a new sound.”

He continued recording as Model 500 and Infiniti and worked with Moritz von Oswald as Borderland. His career also included years onstage at Detroit’s Movement festival.

Saunderson remembered a more personal part of that history: Atkins helping him finish his first record, “Triangle of Love.”

“Juan was the originator of Techno, a true visionary who opened the door for so many of us, myself included,” Saunderson wrote on Instagram.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Big U Case: Feds Cite Vandalized Witness Home & “Rat” Graffiti As Reason To Speed Up Trial
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Big U case prosecutors pointed to a cooperator's damaged home and "rat" graffiti in arguing against another eight-month trial delay.
item.content:encoded:
Big U faces a prosecution warning about witness safety after a cooperator’s home was burglarized and vandalized with “rat” graffiti.

Federal prosecutors described the attack in their October 26 opposition to moving the case from February 16 to October 19, 2027. The home attack had already been cited in April, and prosecutors raised it again to explain their concerns about witness safety.

Prosecutors wrote: “That exposure is not hypothetical. One cooperating witness’s identity has been spread on social media, and his home was vandalized, burglarized, and spray-painted with the word ‘rat.'”

The passage did not identify whoever damaged or entered the home, and it did not accuse Big U of committing that attack.

Prosecutors also invoked the witness-related charges added this summer against the music executive, whose legal name is Eugene Henley Jr.

“[Big U] is now charged with soliciting and attempting to tamper with a witness while detained — conduct alleged to have occurred on and before June 10, 2026, less than three months after the government served its witness and exhibit lists and less than two months after the Court granted the trial continuance.”

Authorities alleged Big U offered two inmates payment to hurt or kill someone identified as Victim-1 and requested that person’s housing layout.

Big U pleaded not guilty in August. The broader racketeering prosecution included allegations involving extortion, his music business and the Developing Options charity.

His lawyers, appointed September 25, sought additional preparation time for extensive evidence and the newer charges, according to the opposition.

The government also cited the burden on a material witness, a person whose testimony the court seeks to secure:

“At least one material witness has lived and will continue to live under court-ordered conditions since April 2026. He, like any other material witness, is not accused of anything. The material witness statute contemplates that such witnesses will be held only as long as necessary to secure their testimony.”

The opposition also asked the court to establish Big U’s own position on any further postponement.

Prosecutors said their planned roster of roughly 50 witnesses included at least one person who would need to travel internationally.

item.title: Kid Rock Defends AI Choir On Eminem Duet As Bill Maher Questions Lost Jobs
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kid Rock explained his AI choir process on Bill Maher's show as the host questioned the impact on singers who could have done the work.
item.content:encoded:
Kid Rock defended using an AI choir on his Eminem duet after Bill Maher questioned what that choice meant for working singers.

On the October 30 episode of HBO’s Real Time with Bill Maher, Rock explained how he built parts of “Heal My Faith.” He said his backing singers were away when he wanted to finish the track, so he turned to software.

“I’m an impatient guy,” Rock said.

He described entering notes and asking for a Southern gospel sound, then trying several options before choosing one he liked. Rock said saving time drove the choice, rather than the cost of hiring a group to sing.

Maher pressed him on whether the process had taken paid work from people who could have sung those parts.

“When the Beatles used a choir, they needed a fucking choir,” Maher said.

Kid Rock compared the change to drum machines and said he still viewed AI as a tool, while supporting rules on its use.

“I see the dangers of it,” he said.

He contrasted that process with “7 Sins,” where three backing singers recorded repeated takes to create the sound of a larger group.

Kid Rock had already discussed using AI for parts of the album before Halfway 2 Jesus came out October 17. In that earlier Billboard interview, he described generated choir and orchestral sounds alongside recordings made with Nashville musicians and his band.

“Heal My Faith” had drawn attention before its release because Rock and Eminem backed opposing sides in the last presidential race. Rock supported Donald Trump, while Eminem took the stage at a Detroit rally for Kamala Harris in 2024.

AllHipHop previously covered the album’s guest switch, which put Lil Wayne on “7 Sins” and moved Eminem to “Heal My Faith.” The switch followed Eminem’s request to return to the song Rock first brought him, according to Rock’s account to Billboard.

Their work together dates back to Eminem’s guest verse on Rock’s 1998 album Devil Without A Cause.

Eminem addressed their partnership on X: “Not about choosing sides, just choosing to make music with my old friend. Praying for all of us.”

item.title: Nicki Minaj Defends White People & Accuses Abdul El-Sayed Of Jealousy
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nicki Minaj accused Abdul El-Sayed of jealousy over a story about his parents days before Michigan's November 3 Senate vote.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj accused Abdul El-Sayed of turning childhood hurt against white people as Michigan voters prepared to choose their next U.S. senator.

Nicki Minaj posted her criticism on X on October 31 after Drew Pavlou circulated a clip from El-Sayed’s appearance on Hasan Minhaj Doesn’t Know. Pavlou framed the exchange as a complaint about white children having advantages.

El-Sayed was discussing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his own parents, rather than using Pavlou’s phrase about white children.

In the episode released October 28, El-Sayed imagined Hegseth as a high school benchwarmer whose parents cheered him on.

He contrasted that picture with his own account of being a starter whose parents never attended his games.

El-Sayed also described growing up as a brown child with a persistent feeling that he had not done enough. He connected that pressure to learning not to take himself too seriously.

Nicki Minaj interpreted the story differently.

“If you listen carefully it’s a misplaced anger at his own parents for not making him feel worthy that turned into raging jealousy of other children who had parents that lifted them up and poured into them. He’s projected all of that onto white people. He needs to mend his heart before thinking about running for any office. White ppl haven’t hurt him. He knows exactly who did,” she wrote.

Hasan Minhaj moved the interview toward campaign strategy after El-Sayed discussed his upbringing, a moment Nicki Minaj singled out in her response.

“Notice how he doesn’t get the satisfaction he was craving when the interviewer simply anchors himself & doesn’t validate that experience. We should all do more of this. Don’t validate anyone’s experience for the sake of temporary bonding,” she added.

In a separate post that day, Minaj also wrote about jealousy.

“Jealousy is not to be taken lightly. Whenever you identify jealousy, know that you’ve just identified a deadly threat. The bible says jealousy is as cruel as the grave.”

The posts followed Minaj’s October 25 appearance at Donald Trump’s rally at McMorran Place Arena in Port Huron, Michigan.

She urged Republican votes and led chants for Mike Rogers, El-Sayed’s Senate opponent, and gubernatorial candidate John James.

El-Sayed, a former public health official, and Rogers, a former congressman, are running for the seat of retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

The outcome could help decide which party controls the Senate for the final two years of Trump’s term.

Michigan’s general election takes place Tuesday, November 3.

item.title: Blueface Says DDG Helped Him Make $1 Million In 90 Days
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Blueface said he earned $1 million from streaming in 90 days and thanked DDG for introducing him to the business.
item.content:encoded:
Blueface said he made $1 million from streaming in 90 days. He credited DDG with helping him get started, from the introduction to the equipment.

“I made a million dollars in 90 days off streaming,” Blueface said in a clip shared on X. “Shout out to DDG for introducing me to streaming.”

The rapper’s claimed payday followed a sharp rise in his live audience over the summer.

Streams Charts, which tracks livestream viewing, counted about 5.42 million hours watched for Blueface in the third quarter of 2026. That was up from roughly 102,000 in the second quarter.

He ranked ninth on the firm’s list for total watch-time gains, adding more than 5.3 million hours. Most of that viewing came from conversation and daily-life content. The Just Chatting and IRL categories made up about 96% of his third-quarter watch time.

His work with fellow rapper and streamer DDG has also extended beyond the screen.

The two were billed together for the second leg of Blueface’s “Fresh Out of Love Tour.” Promotional material from Pop’s Concert Venue pitched the pairing around both rappers’ livestream followings, bringing their online identities into the marketing for their stage shows.

On Kick, creators can earn money from both monthly subscribers and viewers who send tips.

“You keep 95% of all revenue you receive,” the platform tells creators in its published revenue terms. A $5 monthly subscription pays the creator $4.75, with the rest covering processing fees.

The same 95% share applies to its KICKs tipping currency.

The attention has come with disruptions, too.

As AllHipHop previously reported, deputies have responded to numerous swatting incidents, including a gun report at a Santa Clarita business on October 19 while Blueface was live on Kick. Police found no man with a gun at the scene.

A sheriff’s spokesperson reported that Blueface was arrested and booked after allegedly ignoring commands.

That followed an August 23 call about a shooting at King of Crab on Bouquet Canyon Road. Deputies detained Blueface, then released him.

Sgt. Josh Nemeth told City News Service, “Deputies responded, completed an investigation and determined no crime occurred at the location.”

item.title: Elon Musk Calls Kanye West A “World Champion Troll”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Elon Musk praised Kanye West in a new X reply, years after the rapper's posts led to his suspension from the platform.
item.content:encoded:
Elon Musk gave Kanye West a warm character reference on November 1. He called him a top-tier troll years after the rapper’s posts led to his suspension from Musk’s social media platform.

“Kanye has a good heart and is a world champion troll. (Hall of famer),” Musk wrote on X.

The reply came beneath a post recalling Ye’s earlier defense of Musk.

West’s support for Musk has its own history. On October 2, 2018, he visited the College for Creative Studies in Detroit and urged students to ease up on the Tesla chief. A video credited to Erica Heathcote through Storyful showed the rapper standing on a table while addressing the room.

Musk had already written a tribute to West for TIME’s 2015 list of influential people. Rather than focus only on his music, he praised the rapper’s confidence and willingness to challenge people, describing an artist who wanted his audience to question things.

“The dude doesn’t believe in false modesty, and he shouldn’t,” Musk wrote. Later in the tribute, he added, “He’s not afraid of being judged or ridiculed in the process.”

Their public history also included a much less friendly chapter. West’s account was suspended in December 2022 after he posted an image combining a swastika with a Star of David. Musk confirmed the suspension, which followed a violation of the platform’s rules against inciting violence.

X restored West’s account on July 29, 2023. At the time, the company said his account would not earn money from its monetization program, and ads would not run beside his posts.

The debate over Ye’s antisemitic remarks extended beyond social media. In January 2026, he bought a full-page Wall Street Journal ad to apologize for his behavior and renounce his past praise of Hitler. He attributed his actions to an undiagnosed brain injury and untreated bipolar disorder.
